title: Boss: the flaky test report
summary: The quarterly flaky-test report names three offenders. Make each one deterministic and strong: culture, the end of the month, and ties in an ordering.

steps.title: Quarterly report: the top three flaky tests
body: The platform team's report from 30 days of CI runs on `main`:
The fixes you choose must make the tests deterministic **and** keep them catching bugs: each step below plants bugs your new tests must catch. Pick each row for the diagnosis.

testviz.title: 30 days of main, one column per day
testviz.subtitle: red: at least one failure that day

tests.name: InvoiceFormatTests.Total_text
tests.cause: Started failing on day 16, when half the agents moved to a pool with culture **de-DE**. The code formats with the current culture: `€12,50` instead of `€12.50`. The test never ran under another culture, so it never noticed.

tests.name: RenewalTests.Renews_next_month
tests.cause: Fails only on the 31st. The test computes its expectation from `DateTime.Today.AddDays(30)` while the code adds a calendar month.

tests.name: LeaderboardTests.Top_three
tests.cause: Players are loaded from a dictionary in whatever order it gives, and two players have the same score. The test expects one of them first; the order of ties was never specified.

steps.title: Culture: the German build agents
prompt: The formatter was fixed to use the invariant culture. It is compiled beside your tests:
// Always "€1,234.50": the format the PDF template and the accounting export expect, whatever the server's culture.
public static string Total(decimal amount) => "€" + amount.ToString("#,##0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);

Write `public class InvoiceFormatTests` with at least **3** tests, and run at least one of them **under the German culture on purpose** (set `CultureInfo.CurrentCulture` inside the test and restore it in a `finally`). Three planted bugs, one of which goes back to the current culture.

target: public static string Total(decimal amount) => "€" + amount.ToString("#,##0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);

mutants.name: it formats with the current culture again
mutants.hint: The tests run in en-US: switch one test to de-DE.

require.message: One test runs under another culture
Restores the culture in a finally

hints: The test process runs in en-US, so a current-culture bug is invisible until a test changes the culture itself.
`CultureInfo.CurrentCulture = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("de-DE");` inside `try`, and put the old culture back in `finally`, or the next test on that thread inherits it (a new flake).
Use an amount with thousands and a half: 1234.5 must be `€1,234.50`.
steps.explain: Culture is the hidden input that changes when infrastructure changes. Testing under a hostile culture on purpose turns a future production incident into a red test today.

steps.title: The end of the month
prompt: Subscriptions renew one calendar month after the last payment, on the last day of the month when that day does not exist:
public static DateOnly NextDate(DateOnly lastPaid) => lastPaid.AddMonths(1);

The old test computed its expectation from `DateTime.Today`, so it tested a different case every day and failed on the 31st. Write `public class RenewalTests` with at least **4** tests on **fixed dates** chosen for their edges: an ordinary day, the 31st, February in a leap year and in an ordinary year, December. Three planted bugs.
solution: public static TheoryData<DateOnly, DateOnly> Cases => new()
public void Renews_one_calendar_month_later(DateOnly lastPaid, DateOnly expected) => Assert.Equal(expected, Renewal.NextDate(lastPaid));

target: public static DateOnly NextDate(DateOnly lastPaid) => lastPaid.AddMonths(1);

forbid.message: Fixed dates only, no real clock

hints: `DateOnly` cannot go in `[InlineData]`: use `TheoryData<DateOnly, DateOnly>` with `[MemberData]`.
30 and 31 days are right for some months: pick dates where they are wrong (a day in November or December, the 31st of January).
Jan 31 renews on Feb 28 (2026) or Feb 29 (2028); Mar 31 on Apr 30; Dec 20 on Jan 20 of the next year.
steps.explain: Each fixed date is a named edge of the calendar, so the suite tests all of them every run instead of one random day per run.

steps.title: Ties in the leaderboard
prompt: After the report, product decided the rule for ties: **highest score first; equal scores in alphabetical order of name (ordinal)**. The fixed code, compiled beside your tests:
public record Player(string Name, int Score);
public static IReadOnlyList<Player> Top(IEnumerable<Player> players, int count) =>

Write `public class LeaderboardTests` with at least **3** tests that pin the order, ties included. Feed ties in the **wrong** order on purpose: a test whose input is already sorted cannot see a missing tie-breaker. Four planted bugs.
solution: static IEnumerable<string> Names(IEnumerable<Player> players) => players.Select(p => p.Name);

target: public record Player(string Name, int Score);
public static IReadOnlyList<Player> Top(IEnumerable<Player> players, int count) =>

mutants.name: no tie-breaker
mutants.hint: Give three players the same score, listed in reverse alphabetical order.

hints: Compare whole name lists: `Assert.Equal(new[] { "ada", "bob", "cy" }, top.Select(p => p.Name))`.
For ties, give the input as cy, bob, ada with equal scores: only a real tie-breaker turns that into ada, bob, cy.
Ask for fewer players than you pass in, and check the count.
steps.explain: The flake was a missing specification: nobody had decided the order of ties. Once decided, it is one `ThenBy`, and a test with adversarial input order keeps it decided.
